children: Our Bureau Kolkata: ICICI Bank, India's second-largest lender by market capitalisation, reported a 20% on-year growth in second quarter net profit at 14,843 crore, paced by an 18% rise in core net interest income (NII).

Core profitability shrank marginally, with the lender attributing the contraction to the overwhelming diaspora response to India's forex inflow programmes. Profit at the lender, one of the three considered systemically important by the banking regulator, was 12,359 crore in the year-ago period.

Treasury operations led to a 230 crore loss, compared with a 220 crore income in the year ago period, largely on account of a steep rise in the yield on government securities. Net interest margin (NIM) marginally retreated to 4.18%, as compared with 4.36% in the preceding three months. Executive director Sandeep Batra attributed the dip in margin to significant mobilisation in foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits and the investment it made in branch expansion. "There is likely a margin dip in NIM in the third quarter as the impact of FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation has not played out fully," he said. ICICI Bank garnered $18 billion in FCNR(B) using the dedicated regulatory window.

title: ICICI Bank Profit Spurts 20% on NII
